html:
Tobacco, mostly flue-cured Virginia leaf, has been Zimbabwe's main farm export since the early 20th century, and the country is one of the largest producers in the world.

White settlers built large tobacco farms on land set aside under the Land Apportionment Act, and tobacco helped Rhodesia survive sanctions after UDI. Harare's auction floors became among the largest in the world.

After the land seizures of 2000 output collapsed, then recovered as tens of thousands of small black farmers took up the crop, often with finance from Chinese buyers. Curing the leaf uses large amounts of firewood, stripping forests in Zimbabwe.
sum: Tobacco, mostly flue-cured Virginia leaf, has been Zimbabwe's main farm export since the early 20th century, and the country is one of the largest producers in the world.
